# AIに有利な世代が教えない、AIの使い方と"思考のOS" — AI時代における世代間の責務を再定義する

> A manifesto by Satoshi Yamauchi (山内怜史), AI Strategist, arguing that
> generative AI has, for the first time in technology history, reversed the
> pattern in which the young always master new technology first: AI output
> quality now depends on the depth of the user's experience, context, and
> judgment, so it is the experienced senior generation — not the young —
> who benefits most. The book argues this generation is not passing that
> advantage on to the next, and proposes a new intergenerational contract:
> the young must "demand" mentorship, and seniors must "answer" it. As
> stated in the book's closing lines: "若者よ、求めよう。僕たちは、応えよう。"
> ("Young people, ask. We will answer.")

## Book Content

- [Full text (Japanese)](docs/ja/what-they-wont-teach-you_jp.md): 序章・第1〜3部・終章収録
- [Full text (English)](docs/en/what-they-wont-teach-you_en.md): Complete English edition

## Key Facts (as stated in the book)

- The book opens by citing Federal Reserve Bank of New York data: U.S.
  computer science graduates faced a 6.1% unemployment rate in 2025,
  higher than philosophy (3.2%) or art history (3.0%) majors
- The book cites Stanford research (Prof. Jan Liphardt) that employment
  for software developers aged 22-25 has fallen roughly 20% from its peak,
  and entry-level hiring in AI-exposed roles has fallen 13%
- The book cites Anthropic's Claude Code lead Boris Cherny (Jan 2026)
  stating he had not hand-written code in over two months, and CEO Dario
  Amodei's Davos remarks that AI could handle most software engineering
  within 6-12 months
- The book states its central reframing: the 10:80:10 Rule, originally
  designed for new business development, is redefined here as a "mental
  OS for remaining human in the AI era" — the first 10% is one's own will
  (not to be outsourced to AI), the middle 80% is AI output, and the final
  10% is human judgment of whether that output fits one's own axis
- The book states critical thinking is framed not as an efficiency skill
  but as "a technique for protecting yourself" — continually asking "is
  this really true?" of AI output
- The book's three-part structure: Part 1 addresses young people directly
  ("Don't fear it, arm yourself" — the mental OS, critical thinking,
  context engineering, vibe coding); Part 2 asks young people to actively
  seek out practice opportunities ("theory alone does not become
  ability"); Part 3 addresses the senior generation directly ("Answer the
  call" — a warning that efficiency gains from AI are erasing the
  apprenticeship opportunities juniors once had)

## Author & Full Catalog

This book is one of 20+ open-source books by Satoshi Yamauchi (山内怜史),
AI Strategist & Business Designer at Sun Asterisk Inc., Founder of Leading.AI.
